name: Alteplase
route_note: IV bolus plus infusion for stroke, MI and PE; intracatheter instillation (Cathflo) to clear occluded central lines
owner: Genentech (Roche) in the US; Boehringer Ingelheim elsewhere

discovery.note: Human tPA cDNA was cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli, then produced in Chinese hamster ovary cells.

tagline: Clot-dissolving enzyme for acute ischaemic stroke, the first big recombinant drug hit
summary: Alteplase is recombinant human tissue plasminogen activator, an enzyme that converts plasminogen to plasmin to dissolve fibrin clots. It is used for acute ischaemic stroke within a narrow time window, for pulmonary embolism and myocardial infarction, and in low doses to unblock catheters.
mechanism: Alteplase is a serine protease that binds fibrin in a thrombus and converts bound plasminogen into plasmin. Plasmin then degrades the fibrin mesh, dissolving the clot.

Its activity is much greater in the presence of fibrin, giving relative clot selectivity, but systemic plasminogen activation still occurs and bleeding, including intracranial haemorrhage, is the main hazard.
uses: Acute ischaemic stroke (within 3–4.5 hours of symptom onset)
Restoration of function to occluded central venous catheters

history.title: Gene cloned
history.detail: Genentech scientists report cloning and expression of human tPA in Nature.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Activase for acute myocardial infarction.

history.title: GUSTO-I
history.detail: Accelerated alteplase reduces mortality slightly more than streptokinase in acute MI.

history.title: NINDS trial
history.detail: Alteplase within 3 hours of ischaemic stroke improves functional outcome.

history.title: Stroke approval
history.detail: The FDA approves alteplase for acute ischaemic stroke, the first approved stroke treatment.

history.title: Cathflo Activase
history.detail: A low-dose formulation is approved to clear occluded catheters.

history.title: ECASS III
history.detail: Benefit is shown up to 4.5 hours after stroke onset.

history.title: Tenecteplase approved for stroke
history.detail: The FDA approves tenecteplase for acute ischaemic stroke, a single-bolus alternative to alteplase.

facts: Activase was one of the first blockbuster products of recombinant DNA technology.
It is endogenously produced by vascular endothelial cells.

references.title: The NINDS rt-PA Stroke Study Group. Tissue plasminogen activator for acute ischemic stroke. N Engl J Med 1995
